statement: You are given stones, a list of [x, y] positions on a grid, with at most one stone per position.
A stone may be removed if at least one other stone that has not been removed shares its row or its column.
Return the largest number of stones that can be removed.

examples.explanation: All six stones are linked into one group through shared rows and columns, and every group can be cleared down to a single stone, so 5 can be removed.
The four corner stones form one group and the centre stone (1, 1) shares no row or column with any of them. Each group keeps one stone, so 5 − 2 = 3 are removed.
The stones lie on a diagonal, so no two share a row or a column and none can be removed.

constraints: no two stones are at the same position
